title: Potato Chips, Restructured, Reduced Fat, Lightly Salted

content.title: About
content.content: Potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes processed with a restructuring technology that reduces fat content while preserving a crunchy texture. They are lightly salted, making them moderately salty and suitable for everyday snacking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Restructuring technology cuts oil usage to about 30 % of traditional chips.
A golden crisp crust forms thanks to rapid high‑temperature frying.
Salt is added at the end of the process, retaining the natural potato flavor.
These chips are often used as a base for culinary experiments, such as topping with cheese or spices.
Production of this type of chip began in Russia in the early 2000s.

items.title: Reduced Fat
items.content: Lower fat levels make these chips less calorie‑dense compared with conventional varieties.

items.title: Source of Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Contains Vitamin C
items.content: Quick processing retains small amounts of vitamin C, providing antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Moderate Salt Content
items.content: Light salting satisfies sodium needs without excessive intake.

items.title: Crunch without Excess Fat
items.content: Restructuring keeps the crunch while using less oil, making the snack more pleasant.

items.title: Potato Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Salt Intake
items.content: Even light salting should be monitored by individuals with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric Content
items.content: Despite reduced fat, chips still contain calories and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Trans Fats in Oil
items.content: Some manufacturers may use oils with trace trans fats; choose brands labeled ‘no trans fats’.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the chips as a standalone snack, add them to salads for crunch, incorporate them into recipes (e.g., casseroles), or pair with dip sauces. For a healthier option, limit portions to about 30 g.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chips in an airtight package in a cool, dry place away from light. Once opened, consume within 1–2 weeks to maintain crispness.
